reviews.text: Enola Holmes 2 improves on its predecessor and will make you want to see more films set in this franchise. It builds a fascinating new mystery for Enola Holmes and Sherlock Holmes to solve, one that will see both characters grow as they team up
reviews.author: Branyan Towe

reviews.text: A remarkable sequel that gives the audience a lively Holmes to cheer for.
reviews.author: Pallavi Keswani

reviews.text: Enola Holmes 2 maintains the levels of light, adventurous fun of the original, surpassing it due to a much more cohesive, intriguing central narrative, in addition to overall better pacing. Millie Bobby Brown shines as Enola.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: Enola Holmes 2 brings a fresh, fun new case to our screens with improved performances, characterizations, and relationships.
reviews.author: Gissane Sophia

reviews.text: If you enjoyed the first film, you might enjoy the sequel. If you didn’t, this isn’t going to do any wonders for you.
reviews.author: Pramit Chatterjee

reviews.text: Enola Holmes 2 is a massive improvement over the first, not only from an aesthetic standpoint with a series of high-octane action sequences, but from a pacing perspective, as well.
reviews.author: Maxance Vincent

reviews.text: Despite following the same formula as its predecessor, Enola Holmes 2 keeps up the charm and humour with a crafty mystery filled with entertaining twists and turns.
reviews.author: Laura Sirikul

reviews.text: This is featherweight, family-friendly fare ... but that doesn’t detract from its ability to distract, thanks to a fun, fast-moving script, rich production values and director Bradbeer’s willingness to stand back and let star Millie Bobby Brown shine.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: The plot hitches up its skirts and races along from the very first scene and the style and tone very much echo the original with Enola’s occasional cheeky fourth wall breaking...
reviews.author: Paul Mount

reviews.text: Millie Bobby Brown is terrific... I just found it a little long and not quite as brisk as the first Enola Holmes.
reviews.author: Lael Loewenstein

reviews.text: These Enola Holmes films are just great, striking an excellent balance of action, witty humor and a dark edge.
reviews.author: Tim Cogshell

reviews.text: With a terrific cast and solid production, the sequel to 2020’s Enola Holmes makes for fun viewing.
reviews.author: Sameen Amer

reviews.text: Even though it’s a sequel, set in a familiar world with characters who have appeared on screen in countless iterations, Enola Holmes 2 still manages to feel fresh.
reviews.author: Kimber Myers

reviews.text: This plucky sequel is carried on the slender shoulders of Millie Bobby Brown, who proves once and for all that she has the talent to bring in some box office. She might be a Netflix sensation, but always looks supremely comfortable on camera.
reviews.author: Martin Carr

reviews.text: This sequel outshines its predecessor in almost every department. From more interaction with Henry Cavill's Sherlock, to a more interesting and moving story, this installment strengthens the popular franchise for Netflix. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: Enola Holmes 2 triumphantly builds on the first film with added layers of charm, action, empowerment, and even a bit of romance.
reviews.author: Kristen Maldonado

reviews.text: With some creative reinventions of classic Sherlock Holmes characters and a unique lens on true historical events, Enola Holmes 2 is better than the original and may be one of the best Sherlock Holmes movies to date.
reviews.author: Alex Maidy

reviews.text: The action is exciting, the romance is inspiring, the comedy is fun, and overall, "Enola Holmes 2" is a light and entertaining experience. This world is full of potential, and I wouldn't mind seeing more sequels and even spin-offs. Full review in Spanish.
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: An amusing enough period adventure for the targeted family audience, especially tween girls, though some new failings have been added to those inherited from its predecessor.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: While not quite rising to the heights of its 2020 predecessor, this gonzo sequel still manages to effortlessly entertain.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: While much of writer Jack Thorne’s screenplay copies tropes from the previous film, the additional Sherlock Holmes lore that is expanded in this film, and the return of the characters we love, make this adventure well worth taking.
reviews.author: Josh Flanders

reviews.text: Every bit as infectious as the first installment, "Elona Holmes" is one of the most fun film franchises going right now...
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Brown’s efforts or talent cannot be overstated.  Her charm and charisma are the key to making this all work, her confidence and self-effacing performance, totally winning.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: This solid sequel might lack a little of the freshness and zing of the first film, but the central mystery is suitably puzzling and intriguing and there are some clever Bridgerton/modern day Doctor Who-esque riffs on established Conan Doyle-lore.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: Shove over Sherlock – Enola Holmes is back in business in this droll and entertaining sleuthing adventure.
reviews.author: Larushka Ivan-Zadeh

reviews.text: Brown is a wonderful actor who deserves this leading role.
reviews.author: Deepanjana Pal

reviews.text: It may be popcorn – fluffy and insubstantial – but damn if it isn’t enjoyable in the moment. More of that buttery goodness, yes please.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: Helmed by the stellar Millie Bobby Brown alongside the return of the dashing Henry Cavill, this sequel is slightly more mature than its predecessor while retaining that youthful spark of young adult fiction.
reviews.author: Gabi Zietsman

reviews.text: In its second outing, the Enola Holmes franchise maintains the fizz and fun of the first film, while offering a satisfying mystery.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Though this sequel doesn't quite live up to the creativity and excitement of the original, it's still an entertaining, well-acted, and finely-produced adventure.
reviews.author: Jennifer Green

reviews.text: A satisfyingly intricate, peppy addition to a year of whodunits.
reviews.author: Philip De Semlyen

reviews.text: Breezily enjoyable in a Sunday matinee kind of way that is a reminder that family films do not have to be cheaply produced afterthoughts and actually play to the intelligence of its eager audience.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: Enola Holmes 2 is a film that's as charming and spirited as its main protagonist. The game is afoot once more, and the story more enjoyable than ever.
reviews.author: Natasha Alvar

reviews.text: Enola Holmes 2” feels much more elementary, primary, and uninspired.
reviews.author: Rodrigo Perez

reviews.text: Fun, funny, and impressively clever, Enola Holmes 2 is the rare sequel that not only does well by its predecessor but expands on the franchise’s world in meaningful ways.
reviews.author: Rick Marshall

reviews.text: The film works best when the Holmes siblings get together or when Enola remembers her mother's teachings. There's chemistry among these characters... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: Millie Bobby Brown still makes Enola a very interesting character who talks to us directly as she goes about her exciting adventures.
reviews.author: Betty Jo Tucker

reviews.text: Millie Bobby Brown gives Enola the spunk, personality, and attitude to stand apart from her work as Eleven on Stranger Things. Expect some humor with the sibling banter/rivalry between her and Henry Cavill as Sherlock.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: If viewers aren’t taken in by the enthralling mystery, they’ll be won over by Enola’s wit in a sequel which surpasses the original in every way.
reviews.author: Andrew Murray

reviews.text: As Brown builds out her own enjoyable franchise with the help of Cavill, it's clear that the pop-infused period comedy will showcase its confident tone.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: It's heartening to see Netflix and Millie Bobby Brown's spirited franchise retain its charms in the face of the more masculine (and considerably worse) Red Notice and Gray Man-type movies that the streamer is betting big on.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: Enola Holmes 2 is just as charming and well-acted as the first. The story may be too complicated for its own good and a bit on the predictable side, but the journey is sweet nonetheless.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: Brown essays Enola with unrelenting sass and energy. She is, once again, an absolute delight to watch. Her asides from the camera could have seemed forced, but her twinkling eyes and expressive face sell them.
reviews.author: Kshitij Rawat

reviews.text: There are few sequels that manage to be more effective by simply recycling the essential elements of the original film, but that is exactly what happens with Enola Holmes 2.
reviews.author: Juanma Fernández París

reviews.text: A little featherweight feminism and a lotta Millie Bobby Brown keep Enola Holmes 2 from fluttering away in a breeze. So it’s a lot like the first movie, although it’s got a little less shine and fewer surprises...
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: 'Enola Holmes 2' is another delightfully engaging mystery with a grand sense of adventure, a chin-stroking historical touch and many jokes to tickle families.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: Carried by the energy of Millie Bobby Brown, this energetic romp through the underbelly of Victorian London is a fun and compelling mystery.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: A British filmmaker once told me that every British film is about class in some way. With Enola Holmes 2, that truth is brought to the forefront, and you don’t need a detective to figure that out.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: What should be a high-spirited family film instead feels leaden and overstuffed, more concerned with laying the groundwork for a hypothetical sequel than spinning a quality mystery.
reviews.author: Kat Bailey

reviews.text: For all its narrative ornamentation and socially conscious grace notes, Enola Holmes 2 is still basically a kids’ movie about a smart and plucky girl who solves crimes. And what kind of fussbudget could have a problem with that?
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: A rambunctious sequel with heart and a fight, Enola Holmes 2 manages to deliver on everything the first film did and more. In fact, I’m ready for the game to find its feet a third time.
reviews.author: Kate Sánchez

reviews.text: The pairing of actor and role here is just about perfect, and as much a star-making turn for Brown as her breakout performance in “Stranger Things.”
reviews.author: Noel Murray

reviews.text: The rare sequel that improves on the first.
reviews.author: Petrana Radulovic

reviews.text: Enola Holmes 2 does a pretty great job of bringing aspects of Sherlock’s characterization into the world of his sister to make her story feel like it belongs in the universe that Sir Arthur Conan Doyle built.
reviews.author: Rachel Leishman

reviews.text: Fun and ambitious though below its predecessor. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: Those who enjoyed the first movie are likely to enjoy this new entry. While those who couldn't get into the story or characters are unlikely to find anything different to smile at here.
reviews.author: Courtney Lanning

reviews.text: Sherlock and Enola's dynamic is note-perfect, to the point where you don't even miss stick-in-the-mud foil Mycroft.
reviews.author: Natalie Zutter

reviews.text: Enola Holmes 2 takes the mystery of a missing girl and spins a rousing adventure around pivotal historical events. The superb ensemble cast builds on their established relationships with surprising new additions joining a complex narrative.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: [Millie Bobby Brown] retains the same charming personality in Enola Holmes 2 and she’s fun to watch. Except for this time, her appearance alone isn’t enough to save this bloated sequel.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: With “Enola Holmes 2,” much of the series’ charm returns – thanks to the lovely Brown – all while it tries to evolve and grow like its titular character.
reviews.author: Ema Sasic

reviews.text: It's always fun watching such sleuths do their things in these sorts of films, and Brown and Cavill don't disappoint in portraying that.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: With Sherlock's much cooler little sister back to investigate another case, the film cracks the code on the ever-dreaded sequel conundrum.
reviews.author: Shannon Connellan

reviews.text: A sprightly feminist YA offering “Enola Holmes 2” floats along nicely thanks to a solid production and an appealing cast.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: Glossy visuals and Brown's smart, spunky performance never slow down, and never let it down. Bring on Chapter 3.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: The feminist undercurrent of the first film is still there and this is a franchise with plenty of zing left in it.
reviews.author: Ed Potton

reviews.text: Charming and better than the first film.
reviews.author: Jeff Ewing

reviews.text: The game is afoot (again) in Enola Holmes 2, a wonderful showcase for Millie Bobby Brown that this time manages to work the character’s famous brother, Sherlock, more organically into the mix.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: Enola doesn’t just break the fourth wall. She tickles it, winks at it, and tugs at its sleeve. With another actress, this would be annoying. With Brown, it’s charming.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: Has the silty pall of content: scenes often look dreary and move more drearily still; you’d swear in the fight scenes the actors are just taking it in turns to be hit.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: Everything that worked in Enola Holmes is concentrated and amplified in this sequel.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: A cheeky, breezy sequel that's better than the original.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: Pitched perfectly in that sweet spot that a lot of viewers like from their sequels to crowd pleasing popcorn flicks, [it's] one of those movies that gets the old band back together for the same sort of fun that made the original a charming surprise.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: It's a frisky, fem-centric frolic that's also got some serious stuff on its mind—women’s rights, the unity of sisterhood, toxic workplaces, progressive politics and setting young Enola up as a proto-feminist firebrand. Gender fluidity even gets a nod.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: Here is a sequel of the young adult adaptation that is so perfectly cast and completely charming that you will eventually forgive them for another franchise installment with an excessive running time.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: Better plot, mystery & rhythm, with a more important story to tell. Henry Cavill does more as Sherlock than the 1st one, but Enola is the focus, becoming her own person. Exuding charisma, Millie Bobby Brown was born to play Enola. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: All in all, Enola Holmes 2 is a charming and playful romp that maintains the boisterous energy of the first film. It wears its heart on its sleeve while pulling you in for a silly yet undeniably fun experience.
reviews.author: Melody McCune

reviews.text: Offering up the same kind of sleuth schematics and high-flying fun showcased in “Enola Holmes,” I’d argue “Enola Holmes 2” is a stronger picture with a more solid mystery.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: One can’t help but cheer on this Y.A. feminist tale as a welcome addition to the Sherlock Holmes universe.
reviews.author: Beandrea July

reviews.text: Enola Holmes 2 builds on the best elements of Enola Holmes, letting its central characters shine while leaving room for even more character growth should its cast return for a third film.
reviews.author: Maggie Lovitt

reviews.text: It’s noble that the film wants to embrace family and friendship, but it comes at the cost of a stacked cast, an abundance of moving parts to the mystery, forced sequel hooks, and diminishes Enola’s independence #EnolaHolmes2
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Not anything classic, but a pleasing pop hybrid while it lasts — featuring a young lady who knows how to charm, with or without blood on her hands.
reviews.author: Bob Strauss

reviews.text: It’s a romp geared especially towards tweens, but one that certainly holds enough depth to delight their parents as well.
reviews.author: Matthew Huff

reviews.text: Enola Holmes 2 hews closely to the sequel formula by ensuring that it's bigger, louder and more complex than the previous episode, but simply checking those boxes doesn't necessarily make for a better film.
reviews.author: Brent Hankins

reviews.text: The women in this tale are as well voiced as opera divas, as unbowed as suffragettes, and as brilliant as any mastermind.
reviews.author: Sherin Nicole

reviews.text: Yes, the game is afoot…again. And I am completely onboard for more.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Enola Holmes 2 offers all the fourth-wall-breaking fun of the original and is built around a rather interesting and well-architected mystery, one touching on cultural issues.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: Enola Holmes 2 is still quite enjoyable, but it doesn’t leave the same impression as its predecessor.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Deftly blending action, intrigue and a dash of romance, Enola Holmes 2 also champions the emerging women’s rights movement, while remaining faithfully in lockstep with Arthur Conan Doyle’s distinctive style of deductive detective work.
reviews.author: James Marsh

reviews.text: A competent movie that will entertain fans of the first flick, and the gorgeous set designs and costumes are enough to really drag viewers into the world seamlessly.
reviews.author: Callum Crumlish

reviews.text: While the first Enola Holmes proved itself a worthy entry in the Arthur Conan Doyle-verse, this new mystery is neither as sharp nor as satisfying. But you’ll be having so much fun with the characters, it almost doesn’t matter.
reviews.author: Anna Menta

reviews.text: The story in Enola Holmes 2 is secondary to the jokes — a large percentage of which are Brown adorably mugging to the camera — and general vibe, but it isn't without a message.
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

reviews.text: The cast is fantastic and they do what they can with the overstuffed script and quirky dialogue. It isn’t a bad movie, it just feels familiar, slightly predictable, and far too long. Still, fans of the first movie are sure to enjoy this one as well.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: A second-rate mystery with first-class dialogue, Enola Holmes 2 chooses to focus on Sherlock and gives the older brother the biggest revelations. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Randy Meeks

reviews.text: There are a lot of explosions. Which is perfect because, while it’s a story about a detective, Enola Holmes 2 isn’t a detective movie.
reviews.author: Andrew Webster

reviews.text: The writing remains sharp, the performances on point, and the commentary (as before) targeted, all while providing a smart and often-rollicking good time.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: Enola Holmes 2 ends up doing a bit too much plot-wise, but it's still a breezily entertaining detective romp that builds on the promise of the first movie.
reviews.author: Ian Sandwell

reviews.text: Enola Holmes 2 continues the tradition of cozy mystery from its predecessor, with delightful performances from Millie Bobby Brown and Henry Cavill.
reviews.author: Molly Freeman

reviews.text: As for the mystery at the heart of the story, the film is so packed with twists and turns and revelations that it will leave you on the edge of your seat.
reviews.author: Arezou Amin

reviews.text: Enola Holmes 2 is just as much fun as it takes audiences on a different adventure in the newest installment of the hit Netflix franchise.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: The sequel is built to delight the same viewers who approved of the first chapter, delivering a serviceable game for the eponymous character and her more famous sibling.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Enola Holmes is a tonic: it’s fun, energetic and just the right amount of silly. Sherlock is old news: his younger sister is far more engaging, and a hoot to watch.
reviews.author: Vicky Jessop

reviews.text: With a rousing climax and some threequel seeds worked in, the result is an amiably all-ages mystery movie with a dark streak and a worthwhile message, made worthy of its winning lead.
reviews.author: Kevin Harley

reviews.text: An equally boisterous romp that’s equally as hard to remember once it’s over but one that should keep its many fans engaged enough to warrant further sequels.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: While Bradbeer’s first feature was obliged to deliver all the backstory expected from a film clearly designed to kickstart a franchise, “Enola Holmes 2” just feels weighty, bloated, and convoluted. Not at all like Enola.
reviews.author: Kate Erbland

reviews.text: Enola Holmes 2's shortcomings don’t wreck the film — it’s a serviceable sequel — but the tension between the topics the film tackles and the soft-pedaled approach is one that hopefully won’t haunt future projects.
reviews.author: Lovia Gyarkye

synopsis: Fresh off the triumph of solving her first case, Enola Holmes (Millie Bobby Brown) follows in the footsteps of her famous brother, Sherlock (Henry Cavill), and opens her own agency -- only to find that life as a female detective-for-hire isn't as easy as it seems. Resigned to accepting the cold realities of adulthood, she is about to close shop when a penniless matchstick girl offers Enola her first official job: to find her missing sister. But this case proves to be far more puzzling than expected, as Enola is thrown into a dangerous new world -- from London's sinister factories and colorful music halls, to the highest echelons of society and 221B Baker Street itself. As the sparks of a deadly conspiracy ignite, Enola must call upon the help of friends -- and Sherlock himself -- to unravel her mystery. The game, it seems, has found its feet again!
